hints: Focus on what the name tells you, butanoic acid is a 4-carbon carboxylic acid, so start by working out its full molecular formula.
Butanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, which gives a molecular formula of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$.
Now simplify that atom ratio to its smallest whole numbers by dividing through by the common factor to get the empirical formula.
walkthrough:
**Find the molecular formula first**

Think of butanoic acid like a little chain. But means 4 carbons, and oic acid means a $\text{COOH}$ group at the end.

Structure:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$

**Count the atoms**

Now just count them up carefully. You have 4 carbons, 8 hydrogens and 2 oxygens in total.

Molecular formula:
$$\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$$

**Simplify to the empirical formula**

Empirical means simplest whole number ratio. All the subscripts 4, 8 and 2 can be divided by 2.

$$\text{C}_{4/2}\text{H}_{8/2}\text{O}_{2/2} = \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$$

options.A: Correct. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$ is the simplest whole number ratio of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$. Dividing by 2 gives the true empirical formula.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$ would come from miscounting the carbons, perhaps forgetting the carbon in the COOH group is the 4th carbon.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$ is a common trap. It keeps the 4 carbons but loses an oxygen. Remember a carboxylic acid has 2 oxygens, and you must then simplify.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$ has too many carbons. This confuses butanoic acid (C4) with pentanoic acid (C5).
